title: Service level
caption: Service level 85-99 %: total safety stock the LP would hold (73 products, SS = Z x sigma_d x sqrt(8 business days), placeholder review/lead days) against expected stockouts. Current Z = 1.28 (lp.py, 90 %): 485,541 pieces. At 85 % / 95 % / 99 %: 393,149 / 623,940 / 882,451 pieces. Model-implied SKU-months with a stockout per year (normal demand, 4.35 independent weekly cycles a month) fall from 444 at 85 % to 37 at 99 %. Measured on the stored rolling one-step holdout (73 of the products, 1630 SKU-months, 2023-10..2026-02, served model by history length): actual demand exceeded forecast + 1.28 x monthly sigma in 8.4% of months (95 % CI 7.3%-9.6%, bootstrap over SKUs) against the nominal 10 %. Sigma is the LP's own: the SKU's monthly demand standard deviation over its whole history (holdout months included), recovered as sigma_d x sqrt(average business days a month).
verdict_detail: measured monthly exceedance at Z=1.28: 8.4% (95% CI 7.3%-9.6%, SKU bootstrap) vs nominal 10%
criterion: Stockout months are labelled model-implied (normal assumption). FLAWED if the measured monthly exceedance (actual > forecast + 1.28 sigma) has a 95% interval entirely above 10% (Z = 1.28 <-> 90%; analytics/optimization/lp.py:14)

checks.detail: run_lp.safety_stock_for at Z=1.28 equals Z x sigma_d x sqrt(8) summed: True

data_notes: LP inputs are PLACEHOLDERS (analytics/optimization/lp_inputs.py), realistic values the team chose, not SSM's figures: allocation_pct 105, review_days 5, lead_days 3, target_weeks 3, cover_rule aggregate, warehouse_capacity 3.8e+06, default_procurement_cost_per_unit 25, storage_cost_per_unit 0.5.
Pool: Category A with a stored forecast of status 'ok' and MASE < 1 (pipeline gate).
The model-implied stockout months are a formula (normal demand, independent weekly cycles), not a measurement; the measured exceedance is at monthly grain.
